0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Institution on 24 December 1982, after the draft finalized Mechanics Sectional Committee Engineering and Rock approved by the Civil Engineering Division Council.

0.2 The earthwork involved in embankments and subgrades has to be controlled so that the average properties of the soil are equal in quaiity A number of field control methods have been as adopted in design. This standard covers such methods and also gives guidance evolved. for use in various situations. It is suggested that the tests mentioned in this standard are conducted at regular intervals so that the results are available for every 1 000 m2 of earth file. 0.3 For the purpose of deciding whether standard is complied with, the final expressing the result of a test or analysis, The number of ance with IS : 2-1960*. rounded off value should he the same as standard. a particular requirement of this value, observed or calculated, shall be rounded off in accordsignificant places retained in the that of the specified value in this

1.1 This standard covers various methods of field control of compaction and moisture contents of soil for embankment and subgrade. _~_._ _.~______~

IS : 10379 - 1982 2. METHODS APPLICABLE TO NON-GRAVELY SOILS

method, compaction parameters, that is, 2.1 Method I - In this optimum moisture content and maximum dry density are determined according to the procedure described in IS : 2720 ( Part VII )- l980* and IS : 2720 ( Part VIII )-19747. The in-&u moisture content of compacted soil is determined by one of the procedures given in IS : 2720 ( Part II )The field dry density is determined by any one of the metl?ods 1973:. given in IS : 2720 ( Part XXVIII )-19745, IS : 2720 ( Part XXIX )197511 or IS : 2720 ( Part XXXIV )-19721. The test shall be performed after removing the top 5 cm layer of earth. The compaction efficiency is then obtained density-laboratory maximum dry density. by expression of field

2.2 Method 2 - This method allows the determination of the relationship between the embankment moisture content, dry density and the laboratory optimum conGtions without the necessity of measurement of water content and the results can be obtained in less than one hour. This method, as given in IS : 2720 ( Part XXXVIII )-1976"" can be used directly for both moisture and density controls or only density control. 2.3 Method 3 - In certain weathered soils, field moisture content and dry density differ from the laboratory compaction values: In such soils, a test embankment under nearly identical operating conditions for thickness of soil, watering, mixing and compacting is used to determine field moisture content and dry density attainable. The specified layer of soil should be spread on a test strip `3 x 10 m, watered and left for 5 to 30 minutes depending upon type before rolling. The water content is varied in layers within + 6 percent of laboratory values. Each strip is rolled by the roller gnd the density of soil is measured by either of the methods mentioned in 2.1 after every two passes. A graph of the number of passes against dry density is drawn for each water content. A graph of maximum dry density attained when plotted against water content gives field moisture content and attainable field dry density. The trial gives a minimum number of passes of compaction roller which at field moisture content will give maximum dry density.
